utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Kay, are you ready to continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, it will not come as a surprise, but I have to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yesterday when we adjourned we were looking at Exhibit P463.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If that could be put on the screen, please, and turn to page 6, because we'd looked at page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And you will recollect that, Mr. Theunens, the conversation between Dr. Radic and President Tudjman on the 22nd of August, 1995. That's page 5. There we are, page 6. And it's page 9 to 10 in the Croatian language version. And Dr. Juric [sic] in this continuing of the conversation says: "But where is the problem? The problem is when the person elected in civil authority is bad. And that is usually the case. Well, not everywhere. We have a good one in Kostajnica, but the one in Knin is no good. I do not know where he came from; he's a Serb." And the president said: "He's a Serb." Dr. Radic went on that he was told yesterday he was no good for anything. He was told to replace him. And then we get to this passage: "We discussed that as well today, but since this guy is no good, naturally, Cermak has to do everything, and then various problems come up. The county executive gives up, et cetera, so there is a lot of mess in the terrain. I'm telling you this because I have been through that and seen it all over there." And the conversation continues. In your report, Mr. Theunens, where you deal with the civil and military authority and Mr. Cermak's role, when you were writing your report, did you appreciate the difficulties that were thrust upon him as an individual going to Knin with the mission to normalize life in the city?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And for that reason, General Cermak was caused to undertake more civilian missions than he might otherwise have been caused to do, because of the failures of others. Did you appreciate that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That he was caused to take upon himself more responsibilities because of the need to be pragmatic with the situation on the ground. Did you consider that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot express any -- any views as to whether pragmatism or other motives prevailed, but I am aware of -- of documents that indicate that the role of the person that is discussed in the transcript left room for improvement and that is, for example, mentioned on English page 263 of the second page -- second part of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And we looked at the reports yesterday, remember, from the security services, the political information departments, Major Tolj -- or Brigadier Tolj - my apologies to him - and others, as to why Cermak had to get involved in things that weren't on the face it his business. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Shall we now look at the kind of work, and I know you have referred to matters in your report, but some of these issues require a fuller explanation as to the why it came to Mr. Cermak's way. First of all, shall we look at Exhibit D775. This is it a document written by Major Jonjic, the logistics assistant for Knin garrison. It's an undated report, but it could be that it's after 15 days of being in Knin, if you read the text, and it is his report on what happened and the tasks that were being undertaken by him. You recognise this report; do you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do. I believe it is included in my report, but I'm -- I don't know exactly where I have included it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There are two reports by him, and you certainly included one, but I don't know if you included the other. But this report, as we just look at it, and see Major Jonjic who is from the Split Military District, which is right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And that was also discussed in my examination that there was some communication between General Cermak and the establishment commander of Jonjic, in relation to the assignment of Jonjic to the Knin garrison command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And we shall be looking at that because it goes to the issue of Cermak's authority, which you told us yesterday you wanted to comment on, and we will be looking at those orders. But here again is this major from the 306th Logistics Base, Sibenik, and he is working for the benefit of the city, revitalizing the city. On the first page, we see about water into the city, power to the hospital, metal working.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Carpentry, glazing, railways, electrical power, soup kitchen. 14th of September. So I was wrong when I said 15 days; it's after 15 days. That's what I meant to express, so it's at some period after then. The Court can see the provision of food, page 3. On page 3 from the very beginning, Knin was in a disastrous epidemiological condition because of the dirt of the town, lack of electricity, tons of meat left in refrigerators, the need for cleaning the town. As well as that, he organised or we organised cultural and artistic events, welcome for the president, helping church, kindergartens, school. On the orders of General Cermak made myself available to the government's commission, by that, "commission," do you agree, means the housing commission?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We'll look at documents later which will show that. And we can see the first shop was opened. Bread, milk in Knin, other requirements necessary for the life of a city. All these are segments without which a city cannot live. And we have no need to turn to the last page, but it is signed by Major Jonjic, and the Court has already seen this as an exhibit. And it's point that I want to make that when you give your opinion about his civilian/military authority, saying that he was in control of all aspects of civilian life, what you mean is that, in fact, he took steps to try and get the city going which were necessary to try and make order in the city. That's really what it comes to; doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is indeed an important aspect of General Cermak's duties which are described as civilian/military authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And these don't come about from a rule book or some sort of directive, but come about from being just given a general order of normalising life in the city as being the task?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And I would even add of also having received the authority to engage in these activities, aimed at normalizing life in the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I quite agree being told that and sent down there with that as his mission, which is what the documents reflect. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And as I said, it is an important aspect of his mission, based on the documents I reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter 826, which is another Jonjic report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, may I seek clarification of your last question. You said I quite agree being told that, did you have any specific occasion in mind where it was told, because you said this was not about from being just given a general order of normalising life, you said -- at least I understood your question to be being told that that reflects such a general order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. When the president appointed Mr. Cermak, that was his instruction to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were referring to the -- that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Appointment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We've got 65 ter 826. Is this a report that you recognise? It has largely the same content, the same issues. I don't want to go through it page by page. But is this a document that you have seen?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, might this document be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1015, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1015 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next Jonjic document is rather an unusual one, but I'm using it to demonstrate how there were constraints on General Cermak which need to be considered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we call up 2D07-0137, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There are several pages to this document, and we have no need to go through all of them, as they come to the same thing. It's dated the 5th of September, 1995, and it goes to Split Military District Command. It's subject: Consent requested. And it's from General Cermak, signed on his behalf, but it is on the occasion of a visit of a European delegation. We recollect in Jonjic's reports reference to such things. Refreshments along with other programmes were defined by the protocol. The menu specified prosciutto ham ... "we had to purchase it immediately so we did not have time to request your consent." And then we can see General Gotovina kindly gave the consent, and there was an enclosure of the invoice. Let's go to the next page. And there's a series of documents, the first one has come up as the 21st of October, which is the invoice to be collected from this shop, and it's got the date and the amount and Major Jonjic. Let's go to the next page, and that should be the 6th of September, and we can see our prosciutto ham and the amount and what it's all about, the original invoice. And there are further documents in this, ending up with a letter from Jonjic about a record of the delay of the invoice. And why this is in here is a seemingly insignificant matter but shows the constraints actually on his authority that he was not in command of everything. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because this document has to do with logical procedures and does not allow to draw any conclusions in relation to what you call constraints on General Cermak's authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were the logistical matters for the army?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one would expect --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. I'm asking what you they were, not what you expect. What were they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness knows, he can tell us. But I would consider it appropriate to first wait to what he expected. It could be anything, but, at the same time, of course, Mr. Theunens, you are invited to focus your answer on the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, if I jumped in, but I am trying to go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. I understand you and I also don't want Mr. Theunens to be cut off. At this stage when we do not even know what he expects.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the specific procedures that existed between the 306th of Logistics Base of the Split Military District and the Knin garrison command, but normally such assistance, i.e., the provision of food and beverage would be taken care of by the logistics base of the Military District to which the garrison command belongs. So the document then states basically that General Cermak because of urgency could not wait for an authorisation to obtain or to purchase the food and beverage from General Gotovina, and therefore undertook the initiative to purchase of foodstuff and beverage himself, and he is now claiming a reimbursement, which even though I am not a logistical expert, corresponds with what I have seen when I was stationed in the 2nd Guards Regiment in Germany and as a personnel official was also involved in organising certain receptions and other festivities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1016, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1016 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Dealing now with logistics, this part of the aspect of General Cermak's tasks, can we look at 65 ter 2733.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's dated 8th of August, 1995, from the garrison HQ, signed by General Cermak as an order and sent to the commander of the logistics brigade. And we can see here the various aspects of logistics that he is dealing with in this order. I won't read them out as we'll lose more time, but I think everything can see it. First of all, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I do. Could I just see the bottom of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In both languages. Do you recognise it now?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I do. I'm not sure whether I used it, but, yeah, it doesn't look like an unusual document for a garrison commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. It was footnote 982.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yeah. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And I thank Mr. Mak for that. This kind of document which was issued on the 8th of August is one of the first documents issued by General Cermak. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have one document that you're anxious for us to say, and we'll get there, dated the 5th of August, about which there is some mystery. And then all the other documents are dated the 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I'm anxious or not, I don't think that is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm filling in the gaps for you, Because the 8th of August is a day when the first orders are issued.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the document of the 5th has the date of the 5th, but I agree with you that in the numbering this is an inconsistency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have been doing some homework, I see. In relation to this, these are all standard logistic-type tasks; don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it is also in line with the earlier information you provided, in relation to the role of the Knin garrison command in order to -- to normalize life in the city and re-establish certain services. You will need logistics base as well as engineers and other specialized military units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1017, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1017 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 3218.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is dated the 9th of August, 1995, an order concerning carrying out of tasks of provisions, supply and maintenance of materiel, and equipment and concerns the Knin garrison and the Sibenik logistics base, as well as the Zadar logistics base. Again, do you agree that these are all tasks which are required to be undertaken to try and get supplies and services established within the town of Knin?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And as the Knin garrison is part of the Split Military District, General Cermak has to send his order also to General Gotovina, because it concerns units or logistics bases of General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this documenting made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1018, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1018 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a similar order dated the 10th of August, and concerns the Sibenik logistics base taking over a petrol station at the Slavko Rodic barracks. And the supply of fuel and other supplies necessary. Again, a typical and essential part as between the duties of the garrison in trying to establish itself as one of the servicing parts of the Military District. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And to be really specific, it is included in Article 54 of D32 that the garrison command has a responsibility in organizing fuel stations for the units of the district as well as passing units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Absolutely. Correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made a can exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1019, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1019 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Next document is D763.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's the 12th of August, 1995, footnote 1007 for you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. Page 250.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And it concerns the urgent clearing of a military depot in Plavno with the aim of making the return of the population to the settlement as flexible and fast as possible. And the order is to clear the facility and terrain, and we can see it is to deal with mines, explosives, and a commission is appointed, and that the resources be transferred to the logistics base in Sibenik. Now, is this part of the usual duties of the garrison?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can first establish that Plavno is located within the zone of responsibility of the Knin garrison, as it is established in D33. Now, I would say, to the -- to the second aspect of your question, I would say yes. Why? Because this is a military facility which in this particular case has been taken over from the enemy forces who have been left, and that facility may then be used for the benefits of the units of the Split Military District, i.e., it fits in the territorial responsibility of a garrison command, and it could well be that - but I'm not familiar enough with the location of Plavno - that the clearing of this depot will also facilitate I don't know the use of an access road as appears to be suggested in the first -- in the introduction of the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In fact, its terms are for more getting munitions out of there, to making the area safe; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Rather than the Croatian army using the facility.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that the future use of the facility is not specified in the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we turn to the next document, which is 65 ter 2838, which is footnote 1008, same page in your report. And it doesn't have a date on it, but it's the report after they had been there on the previous day, and it was an order by Major Gojevic, in fact, the colonel, Mr. Frkic states that caused guards to be deployed and reconnaissance by explosives experts, and we can see what happened to it and that there is a report on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, out of completeness, may this be made an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1020, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1020 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 853, which is not in your report. It's dated 13th of August, 1995. It's a letter from the medical centre in Knin, sent to General Cermak, and it's a request. And the director of the medical centre, Dr. Viskovic asks for the approval of the assignment of a soldier of the logistics base to the hospital to be an ambulance driver, and he has been doing that job to date and is the only driver we have. Usual job of the garrison or outside the jobs of the garrison?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a military medical centre, I would say yes. Based on the document, it is not a military medical centre, so I would categorise this request - and we don't know whether it has been granted - falling under the duties as civilian authority General Cermak was accomplishing while he was the garrison commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Otherwise known as helping out the community with a soldier, if you can. Wouldn't that be right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's a request. It's not to do with necessarily authority but in difficult times, sometimes people are expected to help out, don't you agree, in an inform way?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But again talking from the military point of view, the reassignment of people even if there are Noble or human motives behind it, has to be regulated by a procedure, and such a procedure involves that orders are given and documents are made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this exhibit -- may this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1021, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1021 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Various other similar documents that I can put into a bar table, Your Honour, rather than spend too long on them as they go to the same issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Talk about bar table documents, Mr. Waespi, did you have an opportunity to review the first bar table -- table with four entries on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, and also the descriptions are -- are accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Accurate and the comments, you do not object to them?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll further proceed with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The last document in this, and it's the hospital again, 65 ter 5517, and for completeness, I'll deal with it.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that is footnote 1002 in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and 1004. So it is a document you recognise.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's dated the 30th August 1995, and General Cermak issues an order to the logistics as well as medical corps about the hospital not capable of functioning independently effective possible reception and transportation of the wounded to major health care institutions, and so he orders an ambulance to be made available and a driver and that they should be helped logistically. Presumably there is no further comment on that document. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in line with the previous document you showed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I produced it for completeness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May it be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1022, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1022 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In your report, you refer to fish farms, because this is an issue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, sorry to interrupt you. Can I ask one additional question. Earlier you said it was quite understandable that a document which you order the support or the assistance from units which are not in the strict sense units of the Knin garrison but are under the command of the Split Military District, that -- for that reason, a copy would be sent to General Gotovina. Now, in view of this last document, I see that there was an order that an ambulance be made available, that a driver should be provided by the 306th Logistic Base, Sibenik and that there is an order to give further assistance, further help. Now, I do not see that this is copied to General Gotovina. It's just the logistic brigade and the chief of the medical corps, I take it, for the ambulance. Is there any explanation, where you earlier explained that that would be the logical thing to do, that is it is not done here and is just for me an example. I'm not saying that I systematically reviewed documents on this aspect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are different possibilities. It could be an omission which I think is not likely, but what I believe is a more likely option that when we look at the date, it is 30th of August so the Knin garrison has been operating already for quite sometime and has also been sending several requests, so a likely option is there has been a coordination between Generals Gotovina and Cermak, whereby General Gotovina authorises General Cermak to direct requests for assistance of units -- excuse me, assistance by units of the Split Military District directly to the units and that General Gotovina has also informed the units, first and foremost the 306th logistics base, that they are to fulfil orders by General Cermak directly without each and every order being systematically submitted or CCed to General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Such an agreement, that is just an assumption.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is an assumption. I have not seen such an agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I was going to go to fish farms, but in view of Your Honours' questioning there and taking up this matter, and I introduced it as fish farms, I will move to another section of cross-examination which Your Honour might find helpful on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I find all of your cross-examination helpful, as from the others, Defence teams. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We'll go to a section now, lack of authority, and I'd like to look at 65 ter 3219 first. Footnote 1053, Mr. Theunens. This is a document dated the 9th of August, and it concerns the need for logistic support, and we see a Colonel Frkic is ordered to be temporarily transferred to the Knin garrison. We may remember him in the previous orders we've just looked at being involved approximate the Plavno munitions. I don't know whether you were able to take on board the name, but this is the first time he surfaces on the 9th of August with this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1023.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1023 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document following this is D759, Exhibit D759, footnote 78 in the addendum. And it's dated the 9th of August, and it's from General Cermak again being an order to the -- or an order and delivered to General Gotovina, the command of the 306th in Split and the -- commander of the Sibenik 306th, both logistics bases, and we know Major Jonjic from the previous documents we have been looking at and saying the need for a logistic support to the Croatian army units and civilian organs of the Knin garrison and considering that situation, so this order is made concerning Major Jonjic. If we move on now to D758. This document is dated the 12th of August, 1995, and it comes from the commander of the 306th Logistics Base in Split. And it describes following General Cermak's order on the 9th of August, as Major Jonjic leaving his duty of his own free will and making himself available to the Knin garrison commander by which the system of command in the 306th has been seriously disrupted. And we see that there is to be a disciplinary procedure, and the content of -- of the letter, and it is sent to the aforesaid person, including General Gotovina. Did you appreciate, when drafting your report, this issue of the lack of authority of General Cermak to make such commands to other units of the Split Military District?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I have addressed this earlier and in the addendum I have also 65 ter 5773, and I believe it has been tendered, where General Cermak explains to the commander of the 306th logistics base that the reassignment of major Jonjic has been authorised by General Gotovina, and this is, as I said, something I mentioned earlier. If the Knin garrison needs personnel or logistics support from a unit from the Split Military District, military logic would mean that General Cermak has to ask the authorisation or has agree as to obtain the agreement of General Gotovina, i.e., the superior commander of this particular unit of the Split Military District, before such a reassignment can take place. And that's exactly what General Cermak explains in 65 ter 5773.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is Exhibit D760 --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- which we can now proceed to. Appearing in the addendum, but your explanation now is not the same explanation that you had in your first report. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, D760, if it is 65 ter 5773, was not included in the version of the report that was filed in December 2007 but is only included in the addendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's what I said. And the explanation of General Cermak not being able to subordinate people without going through the proper procedures was not in your first report, was it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The report that was served as your final expert's report before the Court.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Do you want me to explain or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, shall I put this to you because it leaves the impression that General Cermak is able to make these orders because he is the superior authority and can do this and can do that, without you having provided the full picture of the limitations, so if you could address that issue.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had had D760 at the time of the filing of the final report in December 2007, I would have obviously have included it to explain what I just said here during my testimony; that is that the reassignment of subordinates which belong to another unit can -- no commander in the military can do it. The commander of infantry battalion A cannot reassign or cannot say well, I want a platoon of battalion B without having the consent of the brigade commander, i.e., the next superior echelon, and this is exactly we see here. The only difference is that we have seen a number of documents both for logistical support as well as for personnel, whereby General Cermak, on the basis of the document, issued the order directly without consulting or notifying or having the agreement of the superior commander. And, as I said, I didn't have D760 at the time of the filing of the first version of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This was a document that the Defence put into evidence, but it was a Prosecution document. It was within your database, as you can see, on the heading of the document, and what I'm concerned about is why a document such as this, which may give a full explanation, was unable to be located by you as part of your methodology for the preparation of the report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is included in the addendum, and as far as I am concerned, the addendum has the same value as the report itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the question apparently -- and I'm intervening because I see a similar malcommunication arising. Mr. Kay didn't ask you whether the addendum had the same value or not. Mr. Kay was concerned about if you missed this document in the first report and that it only came up in the addendum. That's what he puts to you, although he didn't ask any question, I take it that he wanted your comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only make the same observation as you do. I mean in relation that it's not included in the final version that was filed in December 2007, but I did not provide an additional explanation. There is no particular reason for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit D769, please. 65 ter 535, a request for vehicles to the transport and technical administration, dated the 11th of August, and we can see the types of vehicles they are, issued by General Cermak to that particular section of the Croatian military. Again, indicating, firstly, that the garrison didn't have these kinds of resources at its disposal when it was started. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the document only states that the garrison wants to have these vehicles. They may have had similar vehicles; I don't know. But this is a request for additional vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know if they had similar vehicles, refrigerator trucks, pick-up trucks, all-terrain vehicles, vans? Do you know? Have you done any research on that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I have not done any specific research on the vehicles of the Knin garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the resources that were available to it? Have you researched that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. I'm asking it again, and please would you do the courtesy of answering. The resources.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am asking about the resources available to the garrison. You have provided an expert report giving your opinion on the position in Knin, and I am questioning you as an expert.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean -- could you please specify the word "resources."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Vehicles at their disposal, computers, telephones.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not done any specific --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Storage?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Storage?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please explain what you mean by "storage."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Resources, where you put things, where you can store things.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not done any specific research on resources, including storage of the Knin garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this -- it's already an exhibit. Can we look now at D761.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Footnote 1053. This is dated the 11th of August, 1995. It's -- concerns operational needs of the Knin garrison, and it's an order by General Cermak temporarily assigning people from the ranks of the 142nd, and we see their names, and he sends it to the 142nd. Do you know if this order was complied with by the commander of the 142nd?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with D764 which is actually an order by General Gotovina to the commander of the 142nd to provide the manpower requested by General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We've looked at D763. And there is another order at D765 concerning the need for people and a request for temporary transfer. Can we see that, please. 22nd of August, 1995, which is footnote 1001. And it's to the 1st Croatian Guards Corps, Colonel General Cuk - apologies if I got his name wrong - request for temporary transfer, and we see various people named there. And it refers in the letter to a Colonel Gregorovic being informed of the request in a letter dated the 15th of August and asking that this be resolved promptly. Was this resolved then, or did it take even more time for this matter to be resolved; do you know?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen a document that allows to draw a conclusion on this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. We will get to one later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question. There was an earlier request with, I think, seven names which Mr. Cermak would like to have available to assist him, and I think it was from the -- was it the -- let me just check. Was it from the 142nd? Now you said, I know of an another document, which is a totally different number of people involved there. So, therefore, when you referred to that other document, which is D - let me just check - D764, you're not talking about seven or eight persons, but we're talk being a totally different number. I think it is all together --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe 30 people, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it refers to a list, and it says the list of military conscripts. Knin is 69, Kijevo is 78. So that -- you -- you linked the two documents. There's a difference in time as well. I think the request was from the 12th of August, and the document you refer to is of the 22nd of August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps not the 22nd. Let me just check. Yes, I think it was. Yes, it was the 22nd of August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see now that I was confused, Your Honours, because the document shown by Mr. Kay refers to the 142nd Home Guard Regiment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I had seen -- I made the link to D764 because it is also the 142nd. But D764 is actually linked to D766.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you did it by mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then I don't have to worry anymore about dates and numbers of conscripts involved. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm not going to do a complicated exercise here of cross-referencing names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but you will understand that if you put a document to Mr. Theunens about seven people, and if he refers to a document of well over 100 people that, at least, it comes into my mind that it may be a mistake or something unexplained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you allow me, the document we see now is from the military point of view a different situation because here General Cermak requests people from a unit, 1st Croatian guard corps, which is directly subordinated to the Main Staff, so this is not a unit of the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say the other one was. You made a mistake when you referred to D764 and the document we find on our screen at this moment is not of the same character because it is a unit not subordinated to General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly. Whereas D764, 766 are subordinated -- or concerned units of the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 22nd of August, if we look at that, D765, request for temporary transfer, the one we were looking at. That's the one on the screen. Sorry, we have been looking at several documents, and I lost my place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometimes I -- otherwise I lose track, Mr. Kay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You see this dated 22nd of August, and the request he makes and the need for it being promptly made. If we go to check the names.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me, the fact that it apparently took more than a week, this also seems like -- I won't say an unusual procedure, but we have a garrison commander who asks for reinforcement in personnel from a unit which is subordinated directly to the Main Staff, whereas it would be more usual from the military point of view that the garrison commander, when he needs additional personnel, seeks that support within the Military District he belongs to. And this can be one of the reasons why, based on this document, it appears that the processing of the request takes more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The names may be important as they may feature in other documents doing other tasks at various times. So we can bear them in mind Vuk, Teskeredzic, et cetera. If we pull up 2D07-0151, we will see the original request which apparently wasn't granted by the 22nd. And it's dated the 15th of August, and it is for Ensign Perkovic who is referred to in that previous document. So 2D07-0151, we can see this was send to Colonel Gregorovic on 15th of August, and the exceptional need, et cetera, concerning pyrotechnical clearance of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Negotiations.

utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.text: Exhibit number D1024, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1024 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 2D07-0153 and 2D07-0155 are the similar requests, Your Honour, which I will bar table so that we save five minutes, if that's -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Put it on paper, describe it, any comment, give it to Mr. Waespi, and then we look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And they are the other two mentioned in that request of the 15th of August 2D07-0157.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to clarify the 1st Guards Corps was a unit which could be used all over Croatia because it is at the highest level. It was also known as the presidential guard, so it is not a unit which is used as in the same manner or the same circumstances as, let's say, the average corps or the average unit; it is an elite unit with particular requirements to the personnel with particular equipment. And again without going into the details of -- of the particular request by General Cermak, the fact that a garrison commander requests human resources from this elite unit is rather unusual. So this could explain why maybe the -- request was not immediately granted or maybe was never granted. It doesn't necessarily mean that the person who makes the request has a lot or -- has more or less authority. It is only related to the fact that it's a special unit with a special subordination for very specific operations, and I believe that is important in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much, and this goes to what Mr. Cermak could or could not do, and 2D07-0157 is a request dated the 19th of August to the guard's corp. May this be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Is that the document we see on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1025, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. D1025 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Kay, do we have to explore at all that at least in this letter we do not see any reference to the task already being performed by the person, whereas in the other letter, it did say he is doing the job already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah. Your Honour, I am avoiding going into too much detail here because it is a broad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not judging you. It's just --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I do as a matter of fact, is making you aware of that I, at least, saw a slight difference, and I leave it to you what the relevance is and whether you want to explore it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next one does have a name of interest. 2D07-0159, also of the 19th of August. And it a request for mobilization to the Ministry of Defence pyrotechnical clearance of the terrain. And amongst the names, we see Brigadier Teskeredzic, whose name we will see in a number of different parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1026, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1026 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And 2D07-0161, a document dated the 19th of August, 1995, to the Rudjer Boskovic institute in Zagreb, and it's a request for relief from employment. And it is the same letter from before but solely involving Brigadier Teskeredzic in order to carry out activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1027, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1027 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 3184.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A document dated 6th of August -- 6th of September, 1995 from General Gotovina to the Knin garrison, and it concerns mobilization of serviceman, our response. And it refers to the fact of a letter addressed to the defence ministry, administration for organisation, reinforcement and mobilisation of armed forces in relation to a request to mobilise Brigadier Teskeredzic, a Colonel Domancic, and a Lieutenant Tomsic, and that had been relayed to the General Staff for an operational assessment whereupon the defence minister was given the request, and he didn't agree to the mobilisation of the individuals. Anything you would like to comment on about that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can find this document on page 261 of part 2. I didn't draw any particular conclusions on the document because it is only one document. If you want I can comment here in the sense that -- again, it is it only one comment so it is a hypotheses I make. If a garrison commander needs additional resources, he would -- I mean resources in the sense of personnel -- he would first ask his -- excuse me, his Military District Commander for that personnel. If then - because we are talking about very specialized personnel - the Military District Commander is not able to provide the personnel, it would be up to the Military District Commander to make the request we saw earlier made by General Cermak to the Main Staff, and then the Main Staff would relay or forward the matter or would give an advice to the Ministry of Defence, whereby then the reply would be transferred in the way as it is done in this document, i.e., from the ministry, to the chief of the Main Staff, to the chief of the Military District, and then to the garrison commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And taking this story further, if the last document could be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1028, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1028 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we see Exhibit D767, which is footnote 1065 but is actually part of this sequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it's a document from General Gotovina on the 20th of September, 1995. Again, referring to the exceptional needs for pyrotechnical restoring of the ground, buildings, and removal of the mines. And says: "Mobilise the following: For military post 3231 Knin," which is the garrison. May we turn to page 2 in the English. You would have seen it already in the Croatian language. We see Brigadier Teskeredzic again, Domancic, Tomsic, and some other names. Where they are to report to, to be received by. And on page 3 the execution of the tasks, following the execution of the tasks, demobilize the conscripts, issue them with certificates, et cetera. So there we are. While you have been looking at these particular documents and we have been following this history of some of these people is to show that General Cermak just couldn't pluck soldiers from the Croatian military system to come and work with him without causing some difficulty. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. The documents we have shown or you have shown indicate that efforts are made to have procedures for the reassignment of personnel be respected, and what I explained in my previous reply is, in my view, confirmed by this order by General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can go to 65 ter 638, which is footnote 1003. I think it might have been made an exhibit, actually, as I look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'm checking right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, it hasn't. It hasn't. It was going to be, but I have to restrict my time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 18th of August, and there had been a request from the garrison in order to ensure the completion of work and establish traffic on the Knin-Gracac route and an order for 30 soldiers to be made available. Page 2, soldiers are made available to the Croatian railways on the 19th of August. Colonel Fuzul responsible for implementation of the order. And it's signed by Brigadier Ademi. Again, is this the appropriate procedure by which extra soldiers would be able to be used for garrison tasks within the military system?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number D1029.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1029 is admitted into evidence. One question, Mr. Theunens, I'm seeking clarification. If we have seen what it took to have the military personnel available to the needs of Mr. Cermak, now, the fact that some people were not yet mobilized, is that a factor which complicates matters, and, if so, what are the powers, and I might have missed something in reading, what are the powers of operational commanders in mobilizing military persons? That is not entirely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, indeed in the previous document we saw that it was the Military District Commander, General Gotovina, who could order the mobilisation of a number of specialized officers. The fact that they have not yet been mobilized of course complicates their availability because they may be accomplishing other important tasks, so if they have to be mobilized even if it's in the very short-term, it will still coast time. I'm not aware of any specific regulations which determine from what level onwards an operational commander has the power to mobilise personnel. I cannot say whether it is already at the brigade commander's level or only at the Military District Commander's level or higher, as the previous document indicates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it true that in one of the previous document, but again we go through them very quickly, so I might have missed something as well. As a matter of fact, a request to have some of these persons mobilized was denied by, I would say, the military administrative level -- at the Ministry of Defence. Could you explain how that one level the request for mobilisation is denied, and then by, apparently, an operational commander that these persons are -- or at least one of them is mobilized.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is unusual when we look at the document in which General Gotovina orders the mobilization because indeed one would expect that it's decided at the Main Staff level or even Ministry of Defence level. utterances.text: And I will go back to fish farms which you refer to in your report, and this section is at page 247 of your report, where you say that Cermak appoints an administrator, and you have got footnote 988 and other personnel, 989, for the fish farm in Knin, and he orders to take control over military farms in the area of the Knin garrison, and Cermak is kept informed of the situation at the fish farm in Knin, which is your footnote 991. You'll see that this is dated the 10th of August, and this is the report. And it describes on 9th of August, the trout farm in Knin being visited by a Mr. Juros, minister of agriculture, Dr. Tadic director of the veterinary administration, Dr. Teskeredzic himself from the Rudjer Boskovic institute, and a Dr. Margus from the Krka National Park for the purpose of ascertaining the general situation in the fish arm in order to carry out measures for the protection of the fish stocks and equipment. Then follows a sorry tale of the farm being broken open, as well as doors, work rooms, ransacked, equipment stolen, laboratory devastated, smashed. No cleaning of the nets and grills. We see on page 2 that the fish had escaped into the sedimentation pool, and prompt measures for repair were required on the 10th, and the cleaning of the pools, feeding of the fish. And we can see Dr. Teskeredzic and a Mr. Modrusan and Mr. Roman and Mr. Margus from the Krka National Park, who with their own hands, did the cleaning, and we see information about the fish. Page three is more information about fry sizes and trout weights; won't go into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we go to page 4. In your report at page 247, you deal with the appointments, and in the last sentence you say: "Cermak is kept informed of the situation at the fish farm." In fact, this is where it all starts, is the report to Mr. Cermak to start it all. You've got it in the reverse order of events.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't think that that changes anything to what is put in the report. He appoints an administrator whether it is following the proposal of Dr. Teskeredzic or not. utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, you're an analyst. You're here as an expert analyst, and in looking these documents, you got it the wrong way round.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't think that the wording of paragraph (e), echo, on English page 247 suggests any sequence or chronological sequence of events. utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it -- unless there's evidence of the -- to the contrary, I would expect such a report to address to him when he is still there. But if it's any -- if it's of any significance, I invite the parties to agree on it. If not, the Chamber might work on the basis as I just expressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY

utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take you back for one second, Mr. Theunens, to the -- to the military farms or the military estates. I'm asking you this because many of the other documents deal with, apparently with companies or -- that are perhaps private, whereas you just confirmed on a question by Mr. Kay that these military estates were owned by or belonged to the army. I'm just wondering how to understand that you used the word "order" in your report, whereas the document itself says "approval." What was there to be approved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could -- could we see the document again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it is your footnote 990, which ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit D01035.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: It is a document where this is an translation issue. Maybe that has something to do with it.

utterances.text: Mm-hm. The translation I used have the ERN 0306-2720-0306-2720. It's ...

utterances.text: But is that an uploaded translation? If not, we might have difficulties in getting it on our screen, because ...

utterances.text: I just read the ERN out for the -- to clarify what is used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see here it is not approval but authorisation. Again, not an order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And an order is mentioned in the first lines: "Pursuant an order of the minister of defence."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is correct, Your Honours, as you noted that General Cermak issues an authorisation, but when I look then at the contents of the authorisation, take control, take care, provide, use, forward, this was again in the context of other documents reviewed from my report and in using my report, for me, the reason to use the expression "order" when I make a reference to this document in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In my question I think I introduced another -- what might be a relevant fact is that was that was opened by the military, so to say take care of your own stuff. Is that an order or is that a ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the military well, when you say to somebody, Take control or take care or even take care of your own stuff, well, the military's function, when I look at the service regulations, D32, the way how it -- a commander or a senior person pronounces this, yeah, instruction, is called an order.

utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY

utterances.text: Yes. That makes sense, and it also makes sense that this is regulated by somebody who is in a position to regulate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.text: Exhibit D1037, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As we have been discussing this afternoon, it is one aspect of normalisation of life which was among one of the tasks of General Cermak as I have described in section 3 of part 2 of my report.
