utterances.text: He wasn't just giving away businesses down there in Knin. This was people who'd come in and established a connection, and their conduct was being authorised, again, to prevent disorder. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what this -- this is what these documents indicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, having dealt with those two in that way, the rest I will bar table and hand to my right. May the last document be made a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay [Overlapping speakers] ... as far as the letterhead is concerned and the translation and rather funny characters, I take it that it's to be ignored.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. It may be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Two originals are there. Might be one of those occasions like we had with the UN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least we can read in the original that it's a Split Hrvatska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If someone would be inclined to improve it, I am not stop them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Oh, it's the reading through the computers of characters from another computer which are, in fact, normal when you look at my page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see this on my screen. I'm glad, Mr. Kay, that are you able to explain computer technicals to this Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I make that an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1038, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1038 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There were some temporary allocations of commercial premises, and these concern temporary use of premises for say four weeks or six weeks as a coffee bar and a buffet bar in Libertas Street, previously known as Marsal Tito's Street. Documents with which I think you're familiar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is, yeah, 65 ter 2292 which corresponds with footnote 985 on English page 246, part 2 of the report, which I believe deals with the matter you just raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. We can look at 65 ter 2464. It is probably the same document in the system twice for all I know, Mr. Theunens, but we're talking about the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 65 ter 2464, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it was the Ministry of Defence requiring certain premises to be allocated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we go to page 2 of this document, it's dated the 24th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it's from Brigadier Vukina who mentions the buffet bar, provisions, sales, and another buffet bar in another street. "We'd like to mention that these commercial premises already being used as organised by the command of the Ministry of Defence headquarters for the sake of higher quality supplies to and the organisation of life for the citizens in the garrison town ..." And we can see it is signed by Brigadier Vukina who was a commander at the HQ in Zagreb. Presumably, something that happens when this area had been liberated and a way of providing an outlet so that people can buy coffee and provisions to prevent stealing and other criminal activities to get goods. You see the point?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, Knin is not an isolated island. There are shops in the wider area but, of course, one would need a car. It's likely that -- there was a necessity to open shops to sell groceries and to have a coffee and snack bar, whether that is allow to people to buy stuff or prevent them from stealing stuff, I think that is outside of my expertise to draw a conclusion on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1039, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1039 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And this is the follow-up to the previous document. It's dated the 27th of September, 1995, from the Knin garrison issued by General Cermak. And it goes to the Ministry of Defence, office of staff administration, ordering the return of those business premises previously mentioned, because these coffee bars and the provisions that the -- the grocery shop, you've mentioned in your report, haven't you, as examples of orders being made by General Cermak?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And again this is under the section "normalisation of life" which is part of -- can be found under the heading "Civilian/Military Authority." I have this document with a different 65 ter, but, in any event, I believe it's included under footnote 987.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's right. It comes in several times in several places this document, so it is difficult for us. If we just go to page 2, we can see what happens. The Croatian army had no need for the use of the premises and Mr. Cermak ordered they be closed and handed over to the Croatian government committee.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the 1st of October, at the latest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1040, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1040 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter 5522, footnote 998. And someone has written: "The president of the administrative board of the association of small shareholders Chromos, a paint company in Zagreb on the 15th September," and they've complained that their property was stolen and driven away to a private firm, and it was machines, raw materials, and it went to a particular company in Pozega, and Mr. Cermak was asked to investigate this incident in order to take steps against war profiteers, and we will look at what he does in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The follow-up document is D505, Exhibit D505, please. The English translation has an error in it which was only picked up when we linked the two documents together, the previous exhibit and this document. We can see it says 19th of August in English, but it is plainly the 19th of September, when we look at the Croatian language document. And it's a letter from Mr. Cermak to the police administration in Knin saying: "We are attaching a memo from the president of the Executive Committee of The Association Of Small Shareholders, Chromos in Zagreb ... sent by mistake to your address." And it concerns the theft of Croatian assets: "Since we are not authorised for such and similar problems, we are, therefore, forwarding the memo to you." This was not a footnote in your report. Had you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And in relation to Mr. Cermak's conduct on this matter, it is entirely appropriate he gets information of a specific crime that is sent to him, and he refers it to the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is it already an exhibit, Your Honour. Thank you. Your Honour, the other documents can be bar tabled so that we do not spend unnecessary time on -- on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In your report, you refer to Mr. Cermak having links with foreign delegations. He is a contact with international representatives, and he is also the point of contact for visits by international delegations; page 258.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we could look at the first of a number of documents which I will bar table. 65 ter 2317.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just to clarify, the section actually starts on English page 254.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a letter from the Deputy Commander for political activity, Captain Tomasovic, of the Split Military District. He writes to the vice consulate of Italy, Mr. Meucci, and it concerns his letter of 10th of August, a visit authorised by the president and to visit the integrated areas of the state, and he's advised upon his arrival to Knin to turn to General Cermak or Colonel Zelic for further coordination in this area. And is this one of many such letters and obligations that were sent to Mr. Cermak. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this specific aspect is discussed on English page 258.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a small correction to the translation. It should be deputy assistant commander for political activity. Tomasovic is the deputy to the assistant commander for political activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1042, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1042 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have seen reference in the reports from the political department and elsewhere about Mr. Cermak being overburdened about conversations between Dr. Radic and the president about him having a lot to do. Those are, in fact, correct assessments of the nature of the work and tasks of this man, Mr. Theunens. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen a document where General Cermak complains about being overburdened with work. And I would expect someone in his position, if, indeed, he gets too many of these visits that are actually drawing his attention away from his core tasks, that he would speak to his superiors to say, Look, I don't have time for all these visits. I have to focus on my tasks. I haven't seen such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Maybe we will be seeing some of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will bar table the rest of the letters under this heading, because they have no need for further analysis, but they go to the generality of the issue I have just put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will wait and see your list, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you prepare that list before you finish the cross-examination, then at least we will know if Mr. Waespi objects to any of them, which, of course, will give you an opportunity to introduce them in any other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you that is why Mr. Mak is doing as we go along which -- it was his idea. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just for the record, Mr. President, we have no objections to D1035 the translation issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is then on the record, and the admission into evidence is -- which was already a final one, does not need to be followed by the replacement of the translation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us now turn to a different subject, which concerns accommodation which you write about in your report; page 247, page 252, page 246, 260, 311, and page 345. Some of those are repetitious passages, I know, Mr. Theunens, but I'm just giving all the ones that I've got here, because the same matter appears in different parts of your report, obviously. Let's look, first of all, to 2D04-0262. This document comes from the service for protection of the constitutional order in Split, dated the 5th of September, 1995, from the chief, Mr. Gabricevic, who writes to General Cermak at the Knin garrison and makes a request for ceding the use of residential accommodation. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I have seen this specific document before. I believe that in my report I refer primarily to requests by the military for accommodation in Knin, i.e., request by military units or organisations to General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let just look at this matter so that this can be seen by the Judges. He receives this letter from the constitutional order. They have offices in Knin. They're in the Knin police administration building. They want to carry out their jobs and tasks, and they ask for two three-bedroom apartments and two two-bedroom apartments from the existing housing fund for the purposes of accommodation of employees, and that's because they travel from Split. That's what the letter is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I have no objections. My version here in -- on my other screen is kind of different. On the top left it has the date in Croatian, so -- which confirms the English translation, but I'm just saying that I do have a clearer version of the original than appears to -- oh, here we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number D1043.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1043 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next document is 2D04-0264. It's dated the 8th of September, 1995. It's a reply to the previous letter from General Cermak to the service for protection of the constitutional order. And they were told that the request regarding the use of residential accommodation for your employees in Knin had been sent to the committee of the Republic of Croatia for the municipality of Knin, which is the competent, obviously, body for administration in Knin. And for additional information, please directly contact that committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that correct, that there was, indeed, run by the Ministry of Interior, a body and organisation that was dealing with the allocation of accommodation to individual requests?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, at least at the time of this document, which is the 8th of September, 1995. I cannot say when this committee was established in the municipality of Knin. I have a reference in my report on English page 246 to the 10th of August where it is General Cermak who takes a decision on the assignment of empty accommodation for temporary uses and that is for the use by the Defence office, MO, the Defence administration which is in line with what I said earlier, that General Cermak takes decisions when it comes to the allocation of accommodation for military purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That was for temporary use is the point that would need to be made there; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned temporary use, so it is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Bearing in mind that Knin had developed a problem, hadn't it, with people illegally taking apartments.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- it is probably the case, but I don't remember seeing specific documents dealing with that issue at that -- at this very stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall we have a look then?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we look -- can that document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number D1044.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1044 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Another example of the temporary reassignment of housing can be found in footnote 995, which is on page 248 of part 2, referring to 65 ter 3498.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we look at Exhibit P514.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Within Knin, there had been apartments, before 1991, owned by the Ministry of Interior which were apartments set aside and for the benefit of employees of the government's Ministry of Interior; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, that is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There was also apartments set aside for the Ministry of Defence, so for the armed forces, and they were apartments that the military were entitled to use, part of their estate.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, there was a whole system of state-owned apartments existing --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in SFRY and continued when Croatia became independent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Between 1991 and the eventual liberation of Knin on the 5th of August, these apartments had been taken over within the period of the RSK government; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For what? The apartments located in Kinin or the territory held by the RSK is concerned, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The apartments were -- they belonged to the Republic of Croatia, but the RSK, so-called government, had taken them over.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that a question or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I answered already. Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't catch your answer to it. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I'm not going into whether they belonged to the Republic of Croatia or whether -- the legal issue of property of SFRY and then going to Croatia, that's not my area of knowledge, so I'm not going into a discussion on that. It is correct that these apartments were owned by SFRY, were taken over by Croatia, and then when the RSK --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I stop you there. We're finding ourselves in a similar situation. Mr. Kay seeks to establish, apparently, with your assistance, whether these apartments were in the RSK time used by the RSK for RSK purposes, and, of course, he is referring to Knin, and, of course, he was not digging into the background of ownership but rather the use. So that at least as I understood was what Mr. Kay was seeking you to confirm or to deny, and the other details seem not to be very relevant at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour, thank you. P514 is under seal. I have just been notified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it should not be shown to the public. And we have to verify whether it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having seen page 2 as I have, it was. It is under seal. I can tell from page 2. If we could have a redaction. Around --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the important thing is whether it was shown to the public. Mr. Registrar confirms to me that it was not shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Okay. Very good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And from your analysis of the documents, would it be right to say that those former state-owned apartments were apartments that people illegally occupied and took over when Knin was liberated?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not analysed this topic in the framework of my report. I know from outside my work at ICTY that this was a delicate issue because some of these apartments were -- I mean, not illegally but legally occupied by people already prior to the establishment of the RSK. They stayed there during the existence of the RSK, and, of course, some of them may have left after the RSK ceased or the so-called RSK ceased to exist, so I cannot answer your question. There were certainly apartments that were illegally occupied, but whether that concerns all the apartments, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the court will be able to see the subject matter of Exhibit P514, I believe, on the screens. It is not going to the public; is that right? Yes. But Your Honours can see it. Yes. And if we just turn to page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any confusion about the question and the answer? You asked about apartments being occupied after the -- after Knin was liberated, and I understand from your position that it was after the 5th of August 1995. In the answer, however, Mr. Theunens refers to what happened after the establishment of the RSK. So he apparently answers the questions in terms of having occupied apartments legally and perhaps already continuing in existing situation in 1991. Is there any way that, Mr. Kay, you are referring to a change in circumstances in occupying apartments in 1995, where the witness may have referred to what had happened in 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, what I'm putting to the witness, Your Honour, is that the Republic of Croatia had a number -- had the ownership right to properties that were owned by government institutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you are looking at the occupation of apartments on from the 5th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where I get the impression from the answer that Mr. Theunens was focussing rather on how apartments were occupied after the RSK was established. That is on from 1991. And I want to clarify whether he misunderstood your question, or whether he -- I just noticed that there seems to be some discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. The question disappeared now. I understood the question being in a very general nature, addressing all the apartments. If the question is that after the 5th of August some or state-owned -- a number of state-owned apartments were illegally taken over by people, then the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes that was the question. And apparently you referred to a different moment in time in your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just looking at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break first. We have a break of -- until five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document, as we go further into this matter, is 2D07-0334. This is a document dated the 14th of September, 1995, from the Kotar-Knin police administration, from the head of police, to the Ministry of Defence, concerning housing issues, the matter we've been talking about, Mr. Theunens. First of all, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm not sure of this specific document, but I have seen similar documents and -- I think of P514 which is referred to on page 252 in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall we look at this document. It recites that on the 26th of August, the ministry, that's the MUP, gave an apartment at a particular address to a police officer, and that apartment is in the possession of the Ministry of Interior, so it's one of their stock of housing that I've been talking to you about, and it had been checked by the fund for housing and communal affairs. Can you tell us what the fund for housing and communal affairs was?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no specific knowledge of this fund. I assume it's a -- a civilian authority, organisation dealing with state-owned housing, among other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know when it was established for Knin?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A conflict emerged between the Croatian army officer, with a name given, and the police officer, and the army man claims he entered first, and there have been arguments about it, and he won't leave. And the chief of police is hoping that a solution will be found for the Croatian army member, obviously so that the police can get their housing back as part of their -- their stock. In relation to the regulation and distribution of these properties, do you know what the system was that was established by the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the system that was established by the Croatian government for the regulation and distribution of state-owned properties. From this document, it appears that the -- the fund for housing and communal affairs plays a role in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1045, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 2D07-034, thia is a document -- 0340, sorry. This is a document dated the 3rd of November, 1995. It is a letter from General Cermak to the government commission for the Knin county housing commission. It's a request for allocation of apartments, and it says: "According to the demonstrated needs for the accommodation of the Knin garrison officers, we hereby request your cooperation in allowing us the use of seven apartments from your housing found on different locations in the town of Knin. "Hoping you will meet our request, we thank you in advance."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Firstly, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no recollection of seeing this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The government commission for Knin county housing commission, what do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no specific knowledge of this civilian body.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You don't know when it was established or ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1046, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We're now going to look at military accommodation, Mr. Theunens. And the first document I would like us to see is 2D07-0318. It's a document from the Ministry of Defence in Zagreb, and we can see there housing commission that is mentioned in the heading. It's dated the 9th of August, 1995, and it's pursuant to the Article 5 of the Law on Temporary usage of apartments and with the consent of the deputy minister. First of all, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know what the Law on Temporary Usage Of Apartments was that he refers to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know what the Law on Temporary Usage Of Apartments is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We see that there is a decision, and it refers to the fact that in the liberated area of the Republic of Croatia, an inspection was to be carried out of all empty, vacant, or abandoned apartments in the property of the Republic of Croatia, which was entrusted with the Ministry of Defence to manage it. Apart from inspecting, there should be an inventory and other -- of furniture and other movables found when inspecting ... a sealing of the apartment to secure it from illegal entry, and the lists of apartments in garrisons is enclosed to this decision, and it is its constituent part. And in paragraph 2: "For listing the apartments and carrying out the inspections in the inventory, the following people were made responsible." If we look at Knin, we see there are 328 apartments and one garage, and a man named Veljko Banek is mentioned. Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing that name before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we turn to page 2. "Listing apartments shall be carried out with another person from the housing subcommission ... in cooperation with the department for construction, military and civil police." That particular subcommission, is that something of which you are aware?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that subcommission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And when listing apartments, pay attention to possible mining of the apartment and inspections to be reported in eight days time. And we can see at the bottom: Delivered to the various people, including responsible persons from the head of the commission, Mr. Adzic, and then there's handwriting on it, concerning the military police, and we saw on the first page, it had gone to the 72nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1047.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document that follows on from this is 65 ter 569. And it's dated the 11th of August, and it's from the Knin garrison, signed by General Cermak. And it's headed: Pursuant to the need of taking over ... apartments owned by the Ministry of Defence ... and with the aim to prevent the appearance of contagious diseases ... And an order is issued about pyrotechnical inspection of the apartments as listed by the building administration, cleaning up of the apartments, elimination of rodents, warnings to be given. We see the names of the people. Page 2, a report was to be submitted by Major Jonjic, and we see building administration, Sector Zadar, et cetera, all on this particular document. First of all, were you aware of a problem in Knin that had developed at this time concerning the health and safety within the apartments that had been left vacant and empty that summer?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I mean, I believe have included this document in my report. Yes, it is footnote 992 on English page 247. And, yes, I think everybody can imagine that people when leave house without planning to leave it, that food, other -- and other stuff may remain in the house. There may have been power cuts, and the consequences of that, yeah, are well known. So the issue of rodents is not unusual in that context, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This order is of Ministry of Defence properties, and we have seen the previous decision by the head of the housing commission, Mr. Adzic, in the previous document, is this part of the duties of the garrison commander, dealing with a matter such as this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say yes. Referring to Article 54 of the service regulations of 1992 which are known as D32, where it is stated under B that the garrison commander -- or the responsibility of the garrison commander include to define the billeting of units and institutions in the garrison and to determine the ordinates of garrison service. I don't see any more specific reference to the issue of keeping military housing in the garrison in an appropriate condition, but in my view, it's in line with the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In fact, this is not billeting, is it, in the accepted military sense of the of the word. These are family apartments?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But these are military apartments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you go to Article 47 of those rules, you will see there accommodation. Lodging and order, yes. Articles 47 and up to 49 were, in fact, outside the garrison regulations, are they not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We Article 47 are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Within the same ones that you were at D32.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the regulation in front of me, so I cannot answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will just leave it as a reference like that. Their Honours can look at it if they need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can this document be made an exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1048.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document is 65 ter 5518. This is a document dated the 16th of August, 1995. Following on from the previous order, it's an order from General Cermak, and it's an order to create conditions for unobstructed work of the housing subcommission of the Knin garrison when patrolling and securing military flats in Knin. "I hereby issue the following," and it's the inspection of military flats for explosives, using carpenters to fix frames and doors, to fit locks. Civilian protection to take rubbish out of flats, carry out pest control, and issuing cylinder locks. A follow-up order on this matter. In line with the -- excuse me, I'm about to sneeze. In line with the duties of the garrison commander or not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1049.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit P1145, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document dated -- Exhibit P1145, that's not what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 65 ter 2389, which is Exhibit D1032. Exhibit D1032, my apologies there, there is an error.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 17th of August from Split Military District Command to the Knin garrison. And it is based on the demobilization of buildings. We've already looked at this already. I'm not sure that we need to look at this any further, as I have questioned you about that. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we have 2D07-0242. It's dated 25th of August, a request from General Cermak to the Ministry of Defence housing commission in Zagreb and a request for allocation of apartments for Knin garrison command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I don't think I have seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's a request to the government Ministry of Defence housing commission to issue a temporary decision on the allocation of apartments in a street for the needs of the Knin garrison. The 14 apartments are to be allocated to the command. "The list of officers will be submitted to you at a later date." Do you know whether this is the correct or incorrect procedure that General Cermak was following, in order to secure housing for members of the garrison command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not able to answer the question. On one hand, one would say, Well, it has to go via the commander of the Split Military District. Now, on the other hand, this is a matter that only concerns the Knin garrison, and it could well be or may well be that can be directly dealt with between a garrison and the housing commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, he is not allocating property himself to people who work for the garrison. We can tell that from the document. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he requests -- I mean he requests in the sense -- he asks the housing commission to allocate, to make available a number of apartments for the needs of the Knin garrison. That is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's just look at it again logically. He is not allocating through his own authority 14 apartments to his unit himself, is he?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. In this document he is not doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's the first point that could be said. Second point is this: That there is a Ministry of Defence housing commission operating in Zagreb that appears to be the place to write to; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1050.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we go to 65 ter 3195, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is footnote 1047 -- not 1047.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 1013, thank you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 252.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. From the housing commission housing sector dated the 6th September, a letter to General Cermak about the unlawful occupation of apartments owned by the defence ministry. And it says, Please have the commander of units located in the Knin garrison - says assembly point here - issue commands banning unlawful entry into apartments belonging to the Defence Ministry of the Republic of Croatia. Our requests submitted hitherto to the political activities service to relay the housing requirements of all their units have not received serious attention with the exception of the Knin garrison, political activities service. We wish to note that the majority of cases in which apartments have been occupied unlawfully is related to senior Croatian army officers from the Zadar military district and other units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you are reading not exactly what appears on our screen, may I draw your attention to the -- with the exception of I have on my screen "the Knin assembly point," but I think you read something different there. Are there various versions, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Assembly point, Your Honours, means garrison. And I know Mr. Theunens knows that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now for the Chamber to -- Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Theunens, isn't it? You knew when I switched into that mode that it was something correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I know. I mean it is an incorrect translation, or probably a literal translation, but literal translations don't always correspond with military terminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Apologies, Your Honour. I thought Your Honour knew that, that's why I did it. If we move on: "We propose that you urgently submit lists of housing requirements for Croatian army members, providing their names, IDs, so that we can propose further measures relating to housing." Go to page two: "Kindly take the necessary steps by the 10th of September. Otherwise, we shall be forced to open up the aforementioned apartments and then seal them off." And then is signed by Veljko Banek, who we saw in the very first order. Remember on the 9th of August, the man allocated to Knin with its 380 apartments and one garage in the first order that I showed you on this section?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote down Baner with an R at the end, but that may be an error on my side. I think it is important to know that this document shows that there is also a housing subcommission within the Knin garrison, so this is a different commission than the civilian commission that exists, for example, at municipal level. Again, I have not analysed these housing commissions as such, but from the heading of the document, left top corner as well as from the formulation used by the author, one can conclude that, indeed, there is such a housing commission dealing with military housing within the Knin garrison command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And this shows that, in fact, the power relating to the allocation of housing through the housing commission, housing sector, is through Mr. Banek's commission.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least at the date of that document, and I believe it is 6th of September?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. At least at that date, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1051.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And just to move on with that point, 2D07-0445. This is a document dated the 15th of September, 1995, from the security an information service at Knin garrison. Remember they were referred to by Mr. Banek -- or he referred to the political activities section; my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a request to that Knin housing subcommission, care of the chief, and it says: "In regard to the housing needs of the security information service, we request from the aforesaid Croatian government subcommission in Knin to allocate 17 flats in total from the Ministry of Defence listing fund, and, if possible, the flats need to be at different locations in Knin."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And it is signed there by the assistant commander. May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1052.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just one word of clarification, I don't know whether Mr. Theunens can answer that, the assistant commander to what, in relation to this document? I see it is blackened out of the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think it is SIS, I should imagine, security and information service.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Within the Knin garrison command. So there is an SIS department or office within the Knin garrison command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, no issue upon that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This document, 20th of September, 1995, again from the Knin garrison. This time it is signed by General Cermak to the housing commission. List of priorities. "And in order to provide accommodation for Knin garrison officers, we hereby submit to you the list of their names for the purpose of issuing temporary decisions." And there we see the list of names which again seems to establish that this is the route for the Ministry of Defence property at this time. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed at 20th of September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if we go to that document you referred to as the 10th of August, 1995, the document you cite in your report, I've got it as 65 ter 2291. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And footnote -- I wrote down the footnote when you cited it, Mr. Theunens, but have I lost it now. When you see the document, you will recollect this is the one you referred to, I believe when we first started discussing the housing issue, that you cite in your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: "Assign a number of empty accommodation units for temporary use ..." So this is the document dated the 10th August 1995, decision by General Cermak on that date. And in order to organise a large number of personnel of the headquarters administration in the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian army in the area of Knin garrison HQ, the decision is issued. It's footnote 985.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: "Assign a number of empty accommodation units for temporary use as needed to the staff of the headquarters administration of the Ministry of Defence so that they can carry out their tasks. "Brigadier Vukina of the headquarters administration is in charge of assigning and organizing the accommodation and issuing provisional decisions," and he is to send an accurate record of the occupied premises including details on the users to the commander of the Knin garrison. Is this the document you were referring to concerning Mr. Cermak's allocation of property?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is one of the examples included in my report. And this is on page 246, this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would you appreciate that in entering Knin in the circumstances that they did and with a large number of military personnel needing to be administered through the headquarters administration, that a temporary use of accommodation units was a practical decision being taken by the garrison commander at the time to try and enable order in the town of Knin?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document states that the aim is -- is to in order to organise a large number of personnel of the headquarters. Of course, that could be considered a component of what is called order or law and order. And it is correct that the person who has the authority to do so is General Cermak, at least at that moment in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And from where did he get his authority?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not -- I have seen the order by the president to appoint him, but I'm not aware having seen a job description for General Cermak that covers the duties he carried out while he held the position of garrison commander in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What we have seen are statements by him, as well as the president as to the nature of tasks, and we've looked at those now through the course of your evidence; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. And there's also other documents included in my report. But we looked at a number of aspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be an exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1045.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that finishing this section, and I would be embarking on a new topic. The witness may have been inflicted long enough with me. I wonder if would be an appropriate just to terminate 15 minutes earlier than usual. It's up to him. But I would be starting a new subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if you think that you would need the next 17 minutes to recover, please tell us. If you think you could continue, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe this is not an answer to the question, Your Honours, but I would need more time to recover. It's not up to me to decide. I can -- I believe at this stage I can manage till the regular ending of court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether you think you could focus and concentrate sufficiently to continue for another 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I can, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Kay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will take a short subject and deal with it that way, rather than embarking on a slightly longer one. And what I'm going deal with is something know as the Podinarje 9, the ASRK soldiers. And you refer in your report at page 242, and this slightly out of sequence from the topics that we have been handling which concern using Knin -- not using Knin, working in Knin. It concerns at page 242 paragraph (J) in your report, that you refer to at least one occasion SJP handover POW, prisoners of war, they take during clearing operations to General Cermak. I'm just interested why you that included as a subject within your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I include it as a subject because, in my view, it contributed to establishing the role General Cermak played when he was the commander of the Knin garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And with that, I don't disagree with you, because the story of the Podinarje 9 begins with them being a group of individuals from the ARSK forces who were still in the Knin region near Unista on the mount Dinara, and they had not surrendered to the Croatian army forces, nor had they withdrawn into Bosnia, but they were still in the region. And they had made contact with a man called Alun Roberts who was the press officer for the UN in Knin, and he was with a number of other UN people who had made contact with them; is that right? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entry in the executive -- in the summary which you cited is based on what I put on English page 292, footnote 1224, and I don't remember exactly whether the information you just provided now is included in the documents that I used in order to establish or provide the information that alleged that nine former members of "paramilitary units of the so-called RSK" were arrested and brought to the Knin garrison command and handed over to General Cermak. It may well be that the information is included, but I don't recall at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know that there had been an agreement between UNCRO and the local Croatian military by the way that any ARSK forces found in the region could be surrendered so as not to get them involved in conflict with the local police or special police or even military themselves? Did you know of that agreement that had been devised between UNCRO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of such an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. Were you aware that it was the three UNCRO military observers with Mr. Roberts who came across this group known as the Podinarje 9 while undertaking their observing missions in that region of Mount Dinara?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And maybe we're talking about a different group, because I'm talking about a group that is, according to a report, by the special police handed over to General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's the same group.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's the same group.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The special police -- the Court has heard evidence about this, Mr. Theunens. The special police came and found the UN observers and Mr. Roberts with this group in the village, and they left the group with Mr. Roberts and the UN observers and withdrew and came back the next day. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware that it was agreement, a brokered agreement, that those nine ARSK soldiers would be taken to Mr. Cermak by the UNCRO observers and Mr. Roberts, and then from him they would be dealt with within the Croatian system as any POWs would be?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of such agreement, and I will check the 65 ter numbers I used --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to see whether they make any reference to such an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that -- that is why General Cermak became involved in this matter, and it is not a case of the special police working under his command or supervision or authority but, in fact, again, it was the matter of UNCRO linking themselves to General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. And I just want it clarify that my report does not suggest that this handover by the SJP implies any authority of General Cermak over the SJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's why I'm looking at it just in case anyone comes to the wrong conclusion. You understand me. I have to guard against that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And let us look to 65 ter 2670.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This doesn't refer to the Podinarje 9, all right, but it refers to a single soldier who was taken custody, and you'll see that it's dated 5th of September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was one of the letters in the bundle that we had from General Cermak to General Forand and was one that I put in that collective to him, so that would have been a bar tabled one that is still out there, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it reads: "I'm extraordinarily pleased that our meeting of 29th of August concerning the voluntary surrender of former members of the Serb army has borne fruit. We are ready to take Mr. Mladen Matic into the custody of Croatian authorities in the presence of UN and other international organisations, as was suggested in your letter." And with a military salute, General Cermak signs off. We have no need to look at page 2. So did you appreciate that there was this background to this issue concerning the surrender of ARSK soldiers who came to UNCRO and then they linked to General Cermak?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned before that I -- I would like to -- I mean, in my time, check 65 ter 1390 and 65 ter 307. Thank you. Just to -- in order to familiarize myself before expressing any views as to whether the document we see now is linked to the group of nine you mention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if we go to -- I'll just go to a couple of documents, 65 ter 3076, 29th of August, 1995. It's from Humo. I don't know who Humo is; it is one that has passed me by in the case so far as a title. Humo, to RC Knin.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say humanitarian officer in ECMM because RC stands for Regional Centre, but again, without seeing the document, just from my background.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Humanitarian monitoring observer, maybe. I don't know. Whatever it is, we can see against the second point in a meeting with HRAT, UNCRO, CIVPOL, UNHCR, ICRC: "The issue of RSK soldiers wishing to surrender was discussed some coordination between IO patrols and CR anti-terrorist groups must be organised. Ideally a UN or ECMM team would monitor the surrender, and info would be directly passed to ICRC for immediate follow-up." And there's the comment: "This was tested this afternoon when nine RSK soldiers surrendered to the HV in the Podinarje valley under UN observation. As the lifeline for hiding RSK soldiers dwindles, increasing numbers can be expected to surrender." Presumably not a document you have been familiar with before.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the framework of the preparation of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the date of 29th is coherent with what -- with what is stated in 65 ter 1390 and 307, because they refer to the 28th, 29th, so, yes, I agree with what you put earlier then in relation to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The connection between the handover of these prisoners of war, on one hand, and the agreement with UNCRO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. The Court has seen other documents, Exhibit P131 as well on this matter, and P37 -- Exhibit P378, Exhibit P48, and that's all I need to say about it. Sorry, that was slightly disorganised. I knew we were talking about the same thing, Mr. Theunens, but I picked a quick subject to get to us 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where we are now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May the last document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1055, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. Mr. Theunens, perhaps I should have asked Mr. Kay as well if he could hold on another 15 minutes, but at least you managed. I to understand that it's quite an exercise you go through at this moment. That may be to some extent true for all of us. We'd like nevertheless to see you back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not tomorrow afternoon. We adjourn, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, 5th of December, 9.00 in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 5th day of December, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
